newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Flood warning issued for Jakarta-paper.
newsitem.headline: Flood warning issued for Jakarta-paper.

text.p: Indonesia's national weather agency warned that Jakarta would be hit by floods in coming weeks because of expected heavy rainfall, the Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Sunday.

"Considering that rainy season continues until March, Jakarta must anticipate and be on alert should heavy rain fall within a short period of hours simultaneously in Puncak-Bogor and Jakarta," the agency said in a statement on Saturday.
Heavy rains in Bogor, 60 km (37 miles) south of the capital, and the nearby hill resort of Puncak usually cause floods in Jakarta -- home to about 10 million people.
"It is feared this condition will lead to even more devastating inundation and floods and could be disruptive to the people in Jakarta," said the agency.
At least 20 people died and 175,000 had to flee when floods hit Jakarta in January and February last year, causing nearly $20 million in damage and briefly paralysing the city.
The rainy season starts in October.
